title: Welder / Welding Fabricator
training_notes: AWS certification (e.g. D1.1 structural) commonly requested by employers; most shops require a hands-on weld test at hire
why_relevant: Direct occupational target of welding program training; core curriculum maps to the occupation's central tasks

title: Structural Metal Fabricator and Fitter
training_notes: Employer-specific fitting standards; larger shops may require rigging or crane signaling awareness
why_relevant: Builds directly on blueprint reading and layout skills; fabrication shops are a common welding-program employer

title: Welding Machine Setter, Operator, Tender
training_notes: Production welding environments; quality documentation practices may be employer-specific
why_relevant: Production-side pathway for students who prefer repeatable machine-driven processes over manual welding

title: CNC Machine Tool Operator
training_notes: Supplemental CNC or machining coursework; NIMS credential often preferred; typically requires dedicated machine training beyond a welding program
why_relevant: Shares precision measurement and blueprint skills; machining shops are significant regional manufacturers

title: Industrial Maintenance Technician
training_notes: Electrical and hydraulic/pneumatic fundamentals usually required; EPA Section 608 or similar may apply in some facilities; often a 1-2 year technical credential
why_relevant: Manufacturers across the region need maintenance capacity; welding skills transfer to repair and fabrication tasks in maintenance roles

title: Quality Control Inspector
training_notes: Quality systems training (ISO 9001 awareness); precision measurement tools (micrometers; CMM exposure)
why_relevant: Weld inspection and quality documentation grow naturally from weld-quality training; manufacturers hire inspectors from fabrication backgrounds

title: Sheet Metal Worker
training_notes: HVAC sheet metal apprenticeships common; licensing requirements vary by state
why_relevant: Layout; cutting; and fitting skills overlap substantially; construction trades offer structured apprenticeship earnings

title: Mechanical Assembly Technician
training_notes: Employer-specific assembly procedures; some roles add electrical assembly skills
why_relevant: Assembly roles are a nearby manufacturing pathway with lower entry barriers; fit-up and blueprint skills transfer

title: Tool and Die Maker
training_notes: Formal apprenticeship (typically 4-5 years) or machinist credential; substantially beyond secondary welding training
why_relevant: Represents the top of the precision metalworking track; shown to illustrate where continued machining training leads

title: Certified Welding Inspector (AWS CWI)
training_notes: AWS Certified Welding Inspector exam; requires qualifying work experience (typically 1-5 years depending on education)
why_relevant: A recognized advancement path for experienced welders; inspection credentials command a wage premium over production welding

title: Manufacturing / Production Supervisor
training_notes: Typically requires several years of shop experience; supervisory and scheduling skills; some employers prefer associate degree
why_relevant: Leadership trajectory that rewards trade expertise; employers commonly promote welders and fabricators into lead/supervisor roles

title: Welding / CTE Educator (Secondary)
training_notes: State CTE teaching licensure; typically requires industry experience plus licensure coursework
why_relevant: CTE programs need instructors with real trade backgrounds; experienced welders can transition to teaching

title: Engineering Technician (Mechanical / Manufacturing)
training_notes: Associate degree in engineering technology commonly expected; CAD proficiency usually required
why_relevant: Shows students the design/engineering side of fabrication; a bridge toward engineering pathways

title: Nursing Assistant (CNA/LNA)
training_notes: State-approved training + competency exam required; completion prepares for VBON two-part test - licensure is granted by the board, not by the course
why_relevant: Direct occupational target of the LNA program

title: Home Health Aide
training_notes: Employer-specific orientation common; home settings add independent-work demands
why_relevant: Documented work setting - home health agencies named in source

title: Medical Assistant
training_notes: Clinical-ambulatory role typically requires MA training or employer-based instruction
why_relevant: Transfers vital-signs and documentation skills into outpatient settings

title: Licensed Practical Nurse (LPN)
training_notes: REQUIRES formal practical-nursing education and NCLEX-PN licensure - an LNA certificate does NOT qualify the holder to practice as an LPN
why_relevant: Natural credential-laddering destination many LNAs pursue

title: Registered Nurse (RN)
training_notes: REQUIRES an accredited ADN/BSN degree and NCLEX-RN licensure - multi-year education pathway
why_relevant: Longer-term pathway; LNA experience strengthens nursing school applications
